scope.excluded: Applying Kowalski's fixed-finite-field Frobenius large sieve from the currently sealed rational finite module, Pluecker incidence, normalized gcd, or CRT recognition alone.
not_excluded: a new compatible bounded-complexity system over a fixed or arithmetic base
a direct horizontal Chebotarev or large-sieve theorem for diagonal congruences
a special exact-zero, Weil-smallness, or auxiliary-local bridge for the actual normalized pair
a rigorously framed sheaf incidence with its own equidistribution theorem

literature_theorem.source: Emmanuel Kowalski, The large sieve, monodromy and zeta functions of curves, arXiv:math/0503714
literature_theorem.result: Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 3.3 give a Frobenius large sieve over U(F_q) for a fixed finite-field base under the stated lisse-sheaf, compatibility or prime-to-characteristic, bounded-twist, linear-disjointness, and uniform cohomological hypotheses.

proved_in_archive: The actual fixed-M tied rows satisfy 4M+1=3p-2s and lie in [(4M+3)/3,(3M-1)/2], an interval of exact length (M-9)/6 and PNT log mass M/6+o(M).
The full residual ceiling is 1/36 per 6M after normalization, and fixed-diameter clusters have only o(M) weight by Item279.
The normalized pair recognizes every full collision by p|Cbar0(M),Cbar1(M), with every affine and rank branch retained.
At fixed M, varying a candidate prime p varies the base characteristic; Kowalski's cited theorem instead averages points of one U(F_q) with q fixed within an application.
The Item273 rational difference module is not a pi_1 representation, and fixed rational singular support is not a uniform l-adic conductor or cohomological-complexity theorem.
The Item275 flag incidence is exact but its natural kernel Pluecker line is non-horizontal; no conjugacy-stable Frobenius local set for the full gate is attached.
No compatible integral auxiliary-ell system, monodromy group, pairwise linear-disjointness theorem, or uniform local-density theorem for the fixed-j=1 endpoint state is currently sealed.
For distinct primes p and ell, p|a,b does not imply ell|a,b; the universal witness (a,b)=(p,p) proves that diagonal divisibility recognition alone gives no auxiliary-ell localization.
A characteristic-p matrix coefficient equal to the gate is still insufficient unless a conjugacy-invariant exact-zero lift or a rigorously framed horizontal theorem is supplied.

Conditionally, if collision forces two conjugacy-invariant compatible integral Frobenius coefficients to be exactly zero, and the complement of their simultaneous auxiliary zero locus has uniformly positive density, then P(L) grows at least as L/log L.
Under the preceding conditional hypotheses, L=q^(1/(2A)) in Kowalski's bound gives |target| << q^(d-1/(2A)) log q.
For the actual horizontal family, N(M)=o(M/log M) implies collision log weight o(M); any power-saving count O(M^(1-delta)) is sufficient.
No implication from Kowalski's vertical bound to the actual horizontal tied family is claimed.
Item149 de-overlap leaves the fixed-j=1 ceiling unchanged at 1/36 per 6M and the new booking at zero.
